integrity.notes: doit.py test-integrity exit 0. The diff against fb040bd only swaps performance.now() for cpuNowMs() at the specified call sites and adds comments, the README sentence, the helper and the new acceptance file. No limits, env names, log text or src/** changed. No special-casing or hard-coded values. Both new acceptance tests fail when the clock is replaced by the wall clock (SPEC-01 fails) or by a constant (SPEC-02 fails), checked in a temp copy. .claude/settings.json is the user's own change, out of scope.

items.evidence: The acceptance test 'does not count time the process spends waiting' passes (313 ms). It asserts wall >= 290 and cpu < 50 around a 300 ms Atomics.wait, and it fails when cpuNowMs is the wall clock. Holdout check through the public export: the value equals (user+system)/1000 from process.cpuUsage; 100k readings are monotonic; a 400 ms setTimeout sleep adds 0.33 ms CPU; a 500 ms Atomics.wait adds 0.06 ms CPU; a fixed workload took 79.7 ms CPU idle and 87.6 ms CPU under 42 busy children while wall time was 208 ms.

The acceptance test 'counts twice the work as about twice the time' passes. It uses sqrt summation, N=20M, warm-up, min of 5, and ratio >= 1.5, and it fails when the clock returns a constant. Holdout check with a different workload (array sorts): 2x work gave a 2.00 CPU ratio and 4x work gave 4.00.

grep over the five files prints nothing (exit 1). The 'bounds the work' block (25 lines) has 0 matches; equity.test.ts has no performance.now or Date.now at all. With 42 busy node processes (3 x 14 cores): the six files with --coverage gave 6 files and 11 tests passed. The exit code was 1 only because of global coverage thresholds (recorded deviation). Evaluator 2.55M evals/s, invariants 0.51 us/action, full ring p95 420 ms. Without coverage, the Run command gave 13/13 passed, exit 0. Full npm test under the same load: 362/362 passed. All busy processes were killed (0 remaining).

Mutation (evaluate does its work twice), idle: the real-target command failed 3/3 on the throughput floor (8.70M, 8.71M, 8.88M < 10M). Reverted; git diff -- src/ is empty. Unmutated, idle: passed 3/3 (15.5-16.1M evals/s, build 31.5-32.1 ms). The locked tests/ci/speed-limits.acceptance.test.ts passed 2/2. CI=true prints 'speed limits not enforced (CI=true)' and passes; an impossible floor without CI fails. However, unmutated under the SPEC-03 load (42 busy processes), the same real-target command failed 6/6, always on the table-build limit: 55.3, 55.0, 53.7, 50.4, 52.0 and 52.3 ms against 50. Throughput also dropped to 10.06-13.9M, close to the 10M floor.
items.expected: Without the mutation, EVALUATOR_MIN_EVALS_PER_SEC=10000000 EVALUATOR_MAX_BUILD_MS=50 npx vitest run tests/engine/hand-evaluator.perf.test.ts passes both idle and under the SPEC-03 load (also stated by the new README sentence: full-speed commands are not failed by a busy machine)
items.actual: It passes idle but fails every run under the SPEC-03 load: the table-build CPU time inflates from about 32 ms to 50-55 ms (about 1.6-1.7x), which exceeds the 50 ms real target
items.observed_via: run command (the README real-target command) with CI unset, with and without 42 busy node processes

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: the unmutated evaluator real-target command (EVALUATOR_MIN_EVALS_PER_SEC=10000000 EVALUATOR_MAX_BUILD_MS=50) passes under 3x core-count busy load, as SPEC-04 and the new README sentence ('including the full-speed commands ... a busy machine does not fail them') state. Actual: it failed 6 of 6 runs under that load on the table-build check (50.4-55.3 ms CPU vs 50 ms; about 32 ms idle). Throughput was also near its floor (10.06M vs 10M in one run).
findings.fix: Under 3x core-count load, the full-speed evaluator command must pass without changing any limit or env default. For example, make the table-build and throughput measurements robust to load-induced CPU inflation, such as the best of several timed repetitions. If the orchestrator or user decides that is out of scope, the spec and the README sentence must stop claiming that the full-speed commands are immune to a busy machine.

summary: SPEC-01, SPEC-02 and SPEC-03 pass with independent evidence, including a full npm test passing at load average about 60 (the original flake is fixed). Integrity is clean. SPEC-04: 2x-slowdown detection and the locked speed-limits test pass, but its stated sub-behaviour that the real-target evaluator command passes under SPEC-03 load fails 6/6 on table build (50-55 ms CPU vs 50 ms), and the new README sentence makes the same claim. One HIGH finding.
